newsitem.title: GERMANY: German cabinet to decide on Eurofighter by Easter.
newsitem.headline: German cabinet to decide on Eurofighter by Easter.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet will decide whether to make a firm order for the Eurofighter 2000 combat aircraft before Easter, German government spokesman Peter Haussmann said on Wednesday.
"A decision will be made before Easter, in the first quarter," Haussmann told a news conference. He gave no further details. Easter falls this year at the end of March.
German Defence Minister Volker Ruehe has struck a deal to pay 23 billion marks for the 180 Eurofighters Bonn wants to buy -- pricing each aircraft at 125.4 million marks.
But, with state finances under extreme pressure from surging unemployment -- which in January touched the highest level since 1933 -- the timing of a decision is delicate.
Ruehe has said he expects parliamentary approval for the purchase during the first quarter, but the timetable outlined by Haussmann indicates a probable further holdup.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel has not yet decided whether to impose a freeze on spending to help Germany meet the Maastricht treaty's deficit goal to qualify for European monetary union, a ministry spokeswoman told the same news conference.
Germany's partners in the project -- Britain, Italy and Spain -- are pressing for Bonn to make a firm order to enable the startup of serial Eurofighter production.
Partners in the project are British Aerospace, Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA), Alenia Spa of Italy and CASA of Spain.
